messages.content: You are reviewing a production autonomous coding harness. Return only the contracted JSON. Find concrete concurrency and cancellation defects; propose the smallest testable design.

Current runtime creates N isolated actors, then for each round dispatches every active actor in one batch and awaits the whole batch before processing any result. A verified actor can satisfy minVerifiedCandidates, but only after every provider in that wave settles. Each actor needs repeated tool/inference turns. The fabric client may enqueue through a persistent spool and polls every 50ms for a settled file; it has no AbortSignal support. Design independent actor progression so a fast actor can take its next turn and reach quorum without waiting for a slow peer. Once quorum is reached, stop client-side polling and stop scheduling new work, while accepting that already-admitted provider work may continue. Preserve isolated workspaces until their actor loop has stopped; do not delete a workspace still in use. State invariants and decisive tests, including a never-settling slow actor.

completion.text: {"design":["Decouple actor execution from polling by using a message queue for actor results.","Implement a priority queue for actors based on their processing speed, allowing faster actors to progress without being held up by slower ones.","Add an `AbortSignal` like feature to gracefully cancel enqueued work for actors that settle or reach quorum.","Maintain a workspace state that tracks whether an actor has completed its processing without deleting until all references are released."],"invariants":["Each actor must maintain its state independent of the other actors' states until their processing completes.","Once quorum is achieved, no new actors shall be initiated while allowing ongoing processes to complete.","A workspace state can be retained without being cleared as long as it's referenced by an active actor."],"risks":["A slow actor may indefinitely delay the processing of results for faster actors, risking a scenario where the system appears unresponsive.","Potential memory leaks if workspaces are not properly managed, especially under rapid churn of actors.","Polling mechanism may introduce latency; if the polling cycle does not catch the settled state of actors, it may miss opportunities to optimize progress."],"tests":["Simulate a scenario with one fast actor and one slow actor, ensuring the fast actor can complete its turns without waiting for the slow actor.","Verify that when quorum is achieved, no new actors are initiated and already initiated work can still process to completion.","Create a test with a never-settling actor to confirm that no resources are inadvertently cleaned up until the actor explicitly signals completion."]}
